site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

run_plan.goal: Critique and validate the UX of the full Booking.com-style booking funnel (search → city list/filters → hotel detail → room selection → reservation details → confirmation) and verify key adjacent flows and recovery points across desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start from index.html, perform a hotel search, validate navigation into the Tokyo/Shinjuku list pages and their filter UX, then open a specific hotel detail and progress through room selection into reservation details and confirmation. In parallel, validate adjacent business-line entry points (flights, car rentals, attractions, airport taxis) plus supporting pages (deals, help, my-trips, register, signin) for consistency, discoverability, and critical error/empty states. Repeat the most failure-prone parts (search controls, filter selection, guest/details form, and final confirmation) on mobile viewport.
assumptions: The site is a static Booking.com clone where navigation between HTML pages represents the funnel states (no real network calls).
The primary booking path likely uses tokyo.html/shinjuku.html → hotel-detail.html → room-selection.html → reservation.html → confirmation.html.
Desktop and mobile variants are supported by responsive layout on each of the listed HTML files.
risk_hotspots: index.html: top search bar controls (destination/check-in-check-out/guests) and the Search button leading to tokyo.html—risk of unclear default state and missing validation feedback.

tokyo.html and shinjuku.html: left filter panels (budget, popular filters, neighbourhood, distance, review score) and empty state messaging (“No properties match your filters”)—risk of non-intuitive filter interactions.
hotel-detail.html and hotel-detail-granbell.html: availability/Reserve CTA placement—risk of unclear how to proceed to room-selection (broken affordance or missing required preconditions).
room-selection.html: “Continue to booking details” and change-selection path—risk of losing context/summary accuracy (dates, guests, cancellation/payment rules).

reservation.html: form completeness for required fields (first/last name, email, country/phone, booking-for choice) and cancellation/payment schedule comprehension—risk of confusing required vs optional, and inadequate validation messaging.
my-trips.html and confirmation.html: cancellation/modify/rebook links—risk of mismatched booking reference or inconsistent state recovery.
signin.html/register.html: authentication entry points from header—risk of navigation loops and missing explanation for where sign-in is required in the funnel.

phases.title: Homepage search & entry-point validation
phases.objective: Validate the primary way users start the journey from index.html: search control clarity, button behavior, and discoverability of major categories and support links.
key_checks: Use the three top inputs: type/select a destination, adjust check-in/check-out dates, and change guest count; confirm the resulting Search action is enabled/works as expected.
Click Search and verify navigation to the expected list view (tokyo.html) without losing the chosen dates/guests conceptually.
Use header/category links visible on index.html (Flights, Car rentals, Attractions, Airport taxis, List your property, Register, Sign in) and confirm each routes to its corresponding HTML page.
exit_criteria: Successful search action demonstrates consistent state handoff (destination + dates + guests) to a city list page.
All visible header/category entry points from index.html reliably navigate to their mapped pages.

phases.title: City list filtering & map/sort affordances
phases.objective: Validate the browsing experience on tokyo.html and shinjuku.html, focusing on filter comprehension, selection feedback, sorting, and empty-results handling.
key_checks: On tokyo.html, interact with at least: budget filter, star rating, one popular filter (e.g., Free cancellation or No prepayment), and one neighbourhood/property-type filter; confirm the UI reflects selected state.
Verify sorting control behavior (e.g., change “Price (lowest first)” vs other visible sort modes) and that hotel cards update accordingly (even if mocked).
On both pages, check “Show on map” (if present via map entry/card) for basic navigation/behavior; ensure no dead-end interactions.
Trigger/validate the “No properties match your filters” empty state and ensure it provides a recovery path (e.g., reset/adjust filters) rather than a dead-end.
exit_criteria: At least one meaningful filter combination is applied and visibly reflected in results.
Empty state is reachable and recoverable with clear user guidance.
Sorting does not break layout or trap the user.

phases.title: Hotel detail → room selection progression
phases.objective: Validate the user’s ability to understand hotel content and confidently proceed from hotel detail to selecting a room and booking details.
key_checks: From hotel-detail.html (Park Hyatt Tokyo), click “Reserve” and confirm navigation to room-selection.html (or equivalent step) while preserving dates/guest selection context.
Use “← Back to results” and verify it returns to the appropriate list context without losing the user’s filtered/browsing state conceptually.

Validate guest trust modules: location rating pill, review count link (e.g., 3,847 reviews) and navigation to reviews.html; confirm reviews filtering controls are usable (e.g., Most recent / Most relevant / Couples).
Repeat Reserve/CTA progression from hotel-detail-granbell.html to ensure multiple hotel details behave consistently.
exit_criteria: Reserve action leads forward to room selection with consistent trip summary.
Back navigation and review entry work without confusing jumps.

phases.title: Room selection summary & booking details entry
phases.objective: Validate the critical step that confirms the user’s chosen room and then gathers required booking details accurately.
key_checks: On room-selection.html, verify the selected room, dates (check-in/out), duration, and price summary (total + key tax/VAT/city tax lines) are readable and match the values shown in the funnel’s later confirmation.
Use “Change your selection” and confirm the user can return to the original selection without losing critical trip context.
On reservation.html, complete the required fields: first name, last name, email, country/region, phone number, and booking-for choice (main guest vs someone else).

Verify required-field guidance (“Almost done! Just fill in the * required info”) is clear and that missing inputs trigger sensible inline validation/disable behavior (or at least visually indicate requiredness).
Confirm understanding sections: payment schedule (“pay at the property / no prepayment”), cancellation policy comprehension, and “special requests” textarea placeholder/wording.
exit_criteria: A fully completed reservation submission action (or the next-step navigation) succeeds to confirmation.html.
Price and policy info remain consistent from room-selection through reservation.

phases.title: Confirmation, trip management, and support/recovery
phases.objective: Validate end-of-flow clarity, post-booking navigation, and recovery/access to support and account-related pages.
key_checks: On confirmation.html, verify confirmation number visibility, hotel/address and room details, cancellation/payment important info readability, and presence of a clear next action (e.g., Manage your booking / My trips).
Navigate to my-trips.html and validate each tab/state (Upcoming/Completed/Cancelled) and primary actions (View details, Cancel booking, Modify dates, Write a review, Book again) are reachable.
Use help.html “Popular topics” (cancel a booking, payment & refunds, change a booking, Genius, transport bookings) and verify topic links/CTAs are usable (chat/call buttons).
From header, validate signin.html and register.html navigation; ensure there is an obvious path for users returning to the booking funnel after sign-in (or at least no broken funnel links).
exit_criteria: Confirmation provides all essential booking details and a plausible path to trip management/support.
Help topics are discoverable and actionable.
Auth pages load cleanly and do not create navigation dead-ends.

phases.title: Adjacent business-line pages (consistency checks)
phases.objective: Validate the alternative booking business lines for basic search/booking CTA behavior and consistent header navigation.
key_checks: Flights: select trip type (Round trip/One way), use origin/destination/date/1 adult, click Search; validate results section presence.
Car rentals: use pick-up/drop-off and date inputs, click Search; validate the “View deal” CTA is present and leads to a plausible continuation.
Attractions: use the top search controls (destination/date range), click Search and confirm “Book now” CTAs exist for attractions.
Airport taxis: fill pick-up, drop-off, date/time, passengers; click Search; validate the list includes “Book” CTAs.
Deals: click “Sign in to unlock deals” and “View deal” entries; ensure they route without breaking layout.
List your property: click “Get started now” and validate informational sections and header navigation.
exit_criteria: Each adjacent page supports its primary input-to-CTA loop (Search/Book) without dead ends.
Header navigation between business lines remains consistent.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages listed in the prescan (run should end having loaded every file in the site's html_files list).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls per key page: index search inputs + Search; tokyo/shinjuku filter groups + sort + empty state; hotel-detail Reserve + back to results + reviews entry; room-selection Continue to booking details + change selection; reservation required form fields + special requests + policy comprehension; confirmation/manage trip navigation; help topics + chat/call buttons; and each business-line page’s primary search/booking CTA.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport for: index.html search controls + Search; tokyo/shinjuku filter selection + empty state; hotel-detail Reserve; reservation form required-field completion; confirmation to my-trips navigation.

notes: Use the most 'funnel-shaped' path for coverage: index.html → tokyo.html/shinjuku.html → hotel-detail.html → room-selection.html → reservation.html → confirmation.html.
Prioritize validation of required-field guidance and price/policy consistency across room-selection → reservation → confirmation, since these are the highest-risk UX points.
Also validate “small tap target” warnings noted on header/auth/support links by checking usability on mobile in phase-1 and phase-5.

Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. ux_notes: Objective achieved: clicking the destination card routed from index.html to tokyo.html (URL changed accordingly).

Trip context appears preserved visually in the header/search bar: destination shows “Tokyo, Japan”, dates show “Tue, Jul 15 — Fri, Jul 18”, and guest summary shows “2 adults · 0 children · 1 room” alongside the “Search” button.

City-list page provides strong filtering affordances and results context (“Tokyo: 6,842 properties found”) with “Filter by:” sections (budget, popular filters, star rating, neighbourhood, property type, review score) and clear quick actions (e.g., hotel cards with prices and “See availability”).

Accessibility/usability signals present on this page: console/network errors are none, but layout warnings indicate small tap targets (e.g., “Booking.com”, “Stays”, “Flights”, etc.) below mobile guidance and an input missing a label/aria-label/placeholder (target ux-10).

step.objective: Learn how the pre-filtered neighbourhood page (Shinjuku) manages filter UI consistency, selected states, and results context compared with Tokyo.
step.success_criteria: The page loads with heading like 'Hotels in Shinjuku, Tokyo' (or equivalent) and shows Shinjuku as the active context, with filters and results list rendered (no blank/error).

ux_notes: Objective achieved: Shinjuku neighbourhood context is clearly active via breadcrumb ('Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku') and page heading ('Shinjuku: 423 properties found').

Filter/results layout appears consistent with the Tokyo page structure: left rail contains grouped filters (budget, popular filters, star rating, neighbourhood, distance, review score) and the right/main column shows sortable/picks and a hotel results list.

Results context messaging is present and prominent: 'Shinjuku: 423 properties found' above the listings and 'Our top picks' dropdown in the same area as results, suggesting consistent secondary context + sorting controls.

Interactive elements are present and actionable: neighborhood filter section includes counts (e.g., 'Shinjuku 423 properties found'), and hotel cards are clickable to details (e.g., Park Hyatt Tokyo, Hotel Gracery Shinjuku, etc.).

Accessibility/tap-size concerns are observable on this page: medium issue 'missing_input_label' for the destination input (ux-10), and multiple low layout warnings indicate navigation links like 'Booking.com', 'Stays', 'Flights', etc. have tap targets below mobile guidance.

step.objective: Check how popular filters behave on the neighborhood results page: selection feedback, results update, and whether the UI prevents dead ends.
step.success_criteria: After clicking the 'JPY 0 - 10,000' checkbox, it should toggle visibly (checked/unchecked), and the 'Shinjuku: X properties found' count and/or hotel cards should update accordingly without navigation away from shinjuku.html.

observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Guest Reviews - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions JPY Sign in Home > Tokyo > Park Hyatt Tokyo > Guest reviews Guest reviews Park Hyatt Tokyo 9.4 Exceptional 3,847 reviews Staff 9.6 Facilities 9.4 Cleanliness 9.6 Comfort 9.5 Value for money 8.8 Location 9.6 Free WiFi 9.2 Breakfast 9.3 All reviews (3,847) Most relevant Most recent Highest score Lowest score All Couples (1,234) Families (876) Solo travellers (543) Business (1,194) TK Takeshi Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 3 nights 10 Absolutely perfect in every way 👍 Liked The views from the 47th floor were breathtaking. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. United Kingdom · Business · Park Suite · 2 nights 9.8 The gold standard for business travel 👍 Liked The suite is extraordinary — separate living area, stunning views, and the bathroom alone is larger than most Tokyo hotel rooms. Club lounge access made early mornings productive. Flawless check-in process. 👎 Disliked Honestly nothing. If I had to nitpick, the in-room coffee machine could be upgraded to a proper espresso machine at this price point. Reviewed: March 2025 YK Yuki K. Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 1 night 8.8 Anniversary celebration done right 👍 Liked They arranged a beautiful cake and champagne for our anniversary without us asking — the concierge noticed it in our booking notes. The Peak Bar at sunset is magical. 👎 Disliked For a one-night stay, the value proposition is harder to justify. The minibar prices are quite high even by luxury hotel standards. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine.
